findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, with an inverted and confusing flag check
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false on both branches. It is a hard-coded kill switch that ignores the feature flag entirely. The logic reads as if it could return true, which misleads maintainers. Anyone who later 'fixes' the inverted condition could re-enable the RCE/LFI path, because the stubbed DB would then be the only barrier. It should be an explicit unconditional error with a comment explaining why.

findings.title: Only the reader path is blocked; other entry points for SQL commands remain
findings.body: The block is applied only in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery. UnmarshalSQLCommand and NewSQLCommand in sql_command.go can still be reached from other code paths, for example the older graph-building path using rawNode. Those paths still call sql.TablesList, which uses the stub DB. They fail with 'not implemented', but the SQL type is not rejected cleanly or consistently. The guard should be placed in NewSQLCommand or UnmarshalSQLCommand so that every entry point is covered.

findings.title: Stub DB returns generic 'not implemented' errors, and TablesList logs the user's raw SQL
findings.body: NewInMemoryDB returns a stub whose methods all return 'not implemented'. In TablesList this error is logged at Error level together with the raw user SQL, and it is surfaced as 'error reading SQL command'. This is a misleading message and noisy logging. The dead parser code (the JSON AST handling and the flatten dependency) stays in the tree even though it can never succeed.
